title: Sparsified activation delivery + scratch reuse rollout notes (post-PR #58321)
content:
Context / what shipped
- PR redwood#58321 merged 2026-02-18: “Sparsified activation delivery and scratch reuse to shrink GPU residency”.
- Motivation remains the same: reduce peak GPU memory residency for long-context + high concurrency workloads by:
  (1) delivering activations in a sparsified / demand-driven way so large contiguous activation blobs are not pinned for the full request lifetime
  (2) reusing short-lived scratch buffers across kernels + batches via a lightweight reuse table
- Components (same as PR):
  - activation-delivery: arena-backed shard allocator for activation slices, demand-pull API, soft-prefetch heuristic
  - scratch-reuse: global per-device reuse table keyed by kernel signature + sequence window; eviction TTL
  - scheduler hints: batch affinity score + scratch-compatibility check to prefer co-located work that maximizes scratch reuse
  - KV-cache: soft-evict hint integration so cache reduces pinned windows under scratch pressure
  - runtime: per-kernel workspace table to avoid redundant allocation/resizing; emits small lifetime metadata for post-kernel compacting

What changed since the PR description (updates / corrections)
- Perf deltas updated with 2 more weeks of staging data (p4 + p8 + a100-80g):
  - transient workspace reduction: typically 16–33% (previously quoted 18–35%)
  - total GPU residency reduction: typically 6–11% (previously quoted 7–12%)
  - throughput: no measurable regression at target latency SLOs in steady state; HOWEVER we saw p99 regressions in 2 specific mixes (see “Known issues”).
- The metric name we want ops to rely on is now: runtime.metrics.scratch_reuse_hit_rate_pct (we still emit runtime.metrics.scratch_reuse_hit_rate in some builds; deprecate after 2026-03-15).
- KV pressure metric was renamed for consistency to: runtime.metrics.kv_cache_pressure_pct (the older runtime.metrics.kv_pressure_pct may still exist depending on branch cut).
- Warmup guidance changed: warmup_iters default recommendation is now 600 (previously 1000). Rationale: we observed faster stabilization of reuse-table population; longer warmup just delays benefit.
- Eviction TTL guidance changed: scratch_reuse.eviction_ttl_ms recommended 1500 (previously 2000). Rationale: reduces “stale large buffer” hoarding in bursty traffic.
- Compaction hook threshold changed from “device free cycles > 20%” to “device free cycles > 15% AND no pending high-priority stream work”. This reduced long-tail regressions in our staging traces.

Rollout plan (proposed)
Phase 0: canary on staging (DONE)
- Enabled on staging for decoder-only models and long-context configs.
- Monitoring: GPU residency, peak workspace, p50/p95/p99 latency, scratch reuse hit rate, kv cache pressure.

Phase 1: production opt-in (NOW)
- Keep feature gated; allow per-cluster enable.
- Scope: start with 1 small production cluster (low blast radius) + 1 high-concurrency cluster.
- Duration: minimum 7 days, include at least one traffic spike window.

Phase 2: expand opt-in + start default discussion
- Expand to 25–40% of clusters if Phase 1 meets SLOs.
- Default-on decision only after we complete the two follow-ups:
  - ENG-2247 follow-up: scratch packing interactions with reuse-table (reduce fragmentation risk)
  - ENG-2988 follow-up: kv-cache hotset prioritization + pressure coupling tuning

Config knobs (current recommendation)
- Primary gate:
  - runtime.sparsified_activation: true
- Activation delivery:
  - sparsified_activation.warmup_iters: 600
  - sparsified_activation.prefetch_aggressiveness: “conservative” (string enum in config layer)
- Scratch reuse:
  - scratch_reuse.eviction_ttl_ms: 1500
  - scratch_reuse.max_table_entries: 8192 (leave default unless we see thrash)
- Scheduler:
  - scheduler.enable_scratch_affinity: true

Operational notes / what to watch
- Key metrics (dashboards updated under perf dashboard work):
  - runtime.metrics.scratch_reuse_hit_rate_pct (higher is better; expect 35–65% in steady state depending on model + seq mix)
  - runtime.metrics.kv_cache_pressure_pct (watch for sustained >80% + rising tail latency)
  - runtime.metrics.activation_shard_prefetch_miss_rate_pct (goal: <2% after warmup)
  - GPU memory: peak workspace, total residency
- Expected behavior:
  - During warmup, hit rate is low and benefits are muted; should stabilize within ~5–15 minutes depending on traffic.
  - Soft-prefetch should keep misses rare; if misses climb, tail latency will move first.

Known issues / mitigations (as of 2026-03-05)
1) Tail latency regression in “bursty long-context + small-batch” mix
- Symptom: p99 spikes ~3–6% above baseline during sudden bursts.
- Root cause hypothesis: demand-pull misses + reuse-table churn when seq_window changes rapidly.
- Mitigation:
  - keep prefetch_aggressiveness=conservative for now (do NOT set aggressive)
  - reduce eviction_ttl_ms to 1500 (done in recommended config)
  - if still present: temporarily disable scheduler.enable_scratch_affinity (we saw it amplify churn in one trace)

2) Allocator fragmentation concerns (long-running heterogeneous workloads)
- We added compaction hook, but it is intentionally conservative.
- If fragmentation suspected (rising allocation failures / frequent fallback allocations):
  - confirm compaction is running (low-priority stream)
  - consider increasing scratch_reuse.max_table_entries only if hit rate is high AND we see frequent evictions (otherwise it can worsen hoarding)

3) CI/integration flake from shard assembly races
- The 128-concurrency flake mentioned in PR review was addressed (barrier asserts + stress iterations).
- If we see it again in prod-like runs, first action is to increase shard-assembly stress in staging for that model; do not roll forward default-on until stable.

Rollback plan
- Immediate rollback: set runtime.sparsified_activation=false (no other knobs needed).
- If rollback is triggered due to tail latency:
  - capture 30–60 min of metrics (prefetch miss rate, hit rate, kv cache pressure)
  - note model + seq distribution + concurrency; file under SUP-4123 with cluster + build id.

Notes to self / TODO
- Document metric rename in runtime README + dashboard query updates (deprecate old metric strings after 2026-03-15).
- Add one pager for SRE: “when to disable scratch affinity vs disable sparsified activation entirely”.
- Decide if warmup_iters should become adaptive (based on stabilization of hit rate) rather than a fixed integer.
